title: Grateful Dead Live at NY State Pavilion, Flushing Meadow Park on 1969-07-11
venue: NY State Pavilion, Flushing Meadow Park
lineage: SBD MC > C  > D > CD + patch from AUD master > low-gen reel > cassette > CD > SHN

ai_review.summary: A historically rare 1969 NY Worlds Fair show with stellar performances (Hard to Handle on pedal steel, Dire Wolf, Dupree’s) captured in a mixed‑source recording that is hissy and uneven but still listenable.
ai_review.review: The concert is celebrated for its unique moments – Jerry’s pedal‑steel on “Hard to Handle,” an early powerhouse version of “Dire Wolf,” a punchy “Dupree’s” and the epic “Alligator” jam.  Reviewers rave about the energy of the New York Pavilion crowd and the historic value, while noting that the audio swings between audience hiss and decent board‑mix sections, making the sound quality only fair.

ai_rating.rationale: The majority of reviewers (≈70%) give 4–5 stars and praise the musical performance; recording complaints are common but do not outweigh the show’s historic and musical strengths.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Several reviewers describe hissy, low‑dynamic audience portions (especially early drums) that switch to a cleaner soundboard mix for the later songs; overall clarity is uneven but the board sections are decent.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Fans note a high‑energy first half with strong jams after “Alligator,” a memorable pedal‑steel rendition of “Hard to Handle,” and a solid second half despite some cuts; the show is described as historic, electric, and full of classic 1969 Dead intensity.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Pedal steel on “Hard to Handle” praised; strong vocals on early “Dire Wolf”; noted for melodic joy during jams.
band_member_comments.Phil: Sings on “Momma Tried”; briefly interrupts Jerry in the intro; generally appreciated by reviewers.
band_member_comments.Bob: Opening jokes are called priceless; occasional vocal contributions noted.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s bluesy organ/keyboard described as crunchy and soulful, a highlight of the era.
band_member_comments.Drums: Multiple reviewers call the drum sound fantastic and one of the best Dupree's drum tracks ever.
